Describe it to the add-content agent, or follow the guide by hand.

install.installer: Installer · Start menu shortcut, can start with Windows

faq.a: Yes. No price, no paid tier, no ads. The code is GPL-3.0-or-later on GitHub.

faq.q: Why does Windows warn me when I install it?
faq.a: The installer is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen shows Windows protected your PC. Choose More info, then Run anyway.

faq.q: Will it slow my PC down?
faq.a: It idles at 0 % CPU and starts at about 24 MB of memory. Nothing runs on a timer while nothing changes.
Any player that shows in the Windows media controls, browsers included.

faq.q: Does it work with several monitors?
faq.a: It sits at the top of one screen: the main one, the focused one, or one you choose in Settings.

faq.q: Does it need an account, or send my data anywhere?
faq.a: No account and no analytics. Four features contact an outside service, each only when you use it: the update check (GitHub, when you click it), synced lyrics (LRCLIB), your calendar link (every 15 minutes) and weather (MET Norway, while that page is on). Settings, the todo list and the shelf stay on your PC.

faq.q: Which versions of Windows does it run on?
faq.a: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit, tested on Windows 11. The media page needs a player that shows in the Windows media controls.

faq.q: Does it show over full-screen apps and games?
faq.a: By default it hides over full-screen apps and shows only lyrics over maximized windows. Settings has behavior options for both: show nothing, activities, lyrics or music. The pin in the open header keeps the notch open over either until you click it again.

faq.q: Can I use it without a mouse?
faq.a: Yes. A touchpad works, and the pages swipe: scroll or swipe two fingers to move between them. While the pointer is on the open notch, the number keys 1 to 9 jump straight to a page and 0 to the last one.

faq.q: Do I need to know programming to add my own page?
faq.a: No. The repository is set up for vibe coding: it ships a guide, docs, an add-content agent, a command that scaffolds the folders and a script that checks your change. Describe the page in plain words, let the agent write it, and the pull request touches only your own files.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy covers the Foldline website and the Foldline app for Windows. Short version: the app has no accounts and contacts no Foldline server, the website counts visits without storing anything on your device, and nothing is sold.

p: Foldline is made and run by one person, Hibatillah ([GitHub profile](https://github.com/hibatillah)). Questions and requests about this policy go through [a GitHub issue](https://github.com/hibatillah/foldline/issues). An issue is public, so do not put personal details in it; ask for a private way to reach me and I will reply there.
The website uses PostHog, set to its US cloud, to count visits. Requests go through this site's own /ingest path, not straight to PostHog.
It records:
ul: Page views and the time spent on a page.
Scroll depth, and where on a page people click (heatmaps).
The referring page, browser, operating system and device type. No location is worked out: the IP address is hashed and discarded.

sections.h: The website: what is not measured
p: No names, emails or accounts: the site has none. No session recordings. Visitors get no person profile, so the events cannot be tied to a named person.

The site stores nothing on your device: no cookie and no local storage, so there is no cookie banner. PostHog runs in its cookieless mode, which counts a visit with a hash it makes on its servers from the request. The IP address is hashed and then discarded, so no location is worked out, and a visit cannot be linked to your other visits or to you.
The language is decided by the address (/ for English, /id for Indonesian); the browser's language setting is ignored and nothing is remembered.

The footer has a Report a bug form. What you type, and the optional contact you add so I can reply, are sent to PostHog as a survey response, read by me to fix the problem and answer you, and kept for up to 24 months. Do not put passwords, secrets or other people's details in it. If you prefer to report in public, [open a GitHub issue](https://github.com/hibatillah/foldline/issues) instead.

The measurements show which parts of the site are used and which break, so they can be fixed. Where a law asks for a legal basis, such as the GDPR, the basis is the legitimate interest in keeping the site working and understanding how it is used. The data is not used for advertising or profiling.
The Foldline app has no account, no sign-in, no analytics and no automatic update check. It contacts no Foldline server. Only these things leave your computer:
ul: Update check: only when you click Check for updates in the settings window. GitHub receives a request for the latest release, with Foldline's name and version in the User-Agent and nothing else about you.
Lyrics: when a track starts, LRCLIB receives the artist, title, album and length. Set FOLDLINE_LYRICS=off to stop lookups.
Calendar: if you set an iCal link, Foldline downloads that file every 15 minutes.
Weather: only with the Weather page on, MET Norway receives the coordinates of your chosen place, at start and every half hour.

p: Settings, the todo list and the shelf are stored in %APPDATA%\Foldline. The clipboard page, when switched on, keeps the last seven copies in memory only; nothing is written to disk or sent anywhere, and the history is dropped when the page is switched off or the app quits. The Copied activity never reads what was copied.

PostHog (website analytics), GitHub (downloads, releases and the update check), LRCLIB (lyrics), MET Norway (weather), and the hosting provider of the website, which keeps ordinary server logs. Each has its own privacy policy. Nothing is sold, and nothing is shared for advertising.
PostHog stores website data in the United States, and the other services above run outside Indonesia too. By using the website you accept that this data is processed in those countries.

Website analytics events and bug reports are kept for up to 24 months, then deleted. The app keeps nothing on a Foldline server, so there is nothing to delete there; your local files stay until you remove them.

You can ask to see, correct or delete data about you, to object to its use, and to complain to the data protection authority where you live. Because visitors get no profile and the data carries no name, I cannot pick out one visitor's events unless you give me something that identifies them. Ask through a GitHub issue as described above.
The website is served over HTTPS. The app keeps your data on your own computer, which is why there is no Foldline server to breach. No system is perfectly secure.
Foldline is not aimed at children, and the website does not knowingly collect personal data from them.
The website links to GitHub and other sites. Their privacy practices are theirs, not covered here.
When this policy changes, the new text replaces this page and the date at the top changes. A change that affects what is collected is noted at the top of the page for 30 days.

This policy is governed by the law of Indonesia, including Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection. The site is open to visitors from anywhere, and rights you have under the law where you live still apply.

releases.title: Releases
releases.intro: What changed in each version of Foldline, in plain words. The full list of changes for every release is on GitHub.
releases.signing: The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows asks you to confirm it.

entries.lead: The first release under the Foldline name: free, open source under the GPL, and with no accounts at all.

items.d: The About page in Settings has an update card. Click its button and Foldline asks GitHub for the newest release. It never checks by itself.
The tray menu can hide notification banners and page alerts for 10 minutes, 30 minutes, an hour, or until you switch it off.
The installer offers to start Foldline when Windows starts. It is on by default.
A notification card shows the icon of the app that sent it.
A page, an activity or a page's settings now lives in its own folder. A script sets it up and checks that a pull request touches only your files.
The app is now called Foldline and is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. Accounts, sign-in and locked pages are gone: every page and activity is free.
Foldline now keeps its files in %APPDATA%\Foldline and copies your settings over from the old folder once, the first time it starts.
Releases are published on GitHub only. Foldline is not on the Microsoft Store.
Foldline ranks the lyric results by length, title and album, and skips lyrics timed for a longer recording.
If the app is already running, its window now comes to the front instead of Foldline starting a second copy.

download.title: Your download is starting
download.subtitle: Foldline for Windows 10 and 11. Your browser and Windows may warn you about the file, so read the steps below first.
download.stepsTitle: What to do when the warnings appear
download.stepsIntro: You will see up to two warnings, one from the browser and one from Windows. Both can be passed:

steps.p: Chrome and Edge may say the file is not commonly downloaded or could be harmful. Open the downloads list, open the menu of the file and choose **Keep**. Edge may ask once more: choose **Keep anyway**.
Run the file you downloaded. Windows may show a blue window that says **Windows protected your PC** (**Microsoft Defender SmartScreen**). Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
Follow the installer. Foldline starts when it finishes and appears at the top of your screen.
Every release lists a SHA-256 checksum for the installer. In PowerShell, run Get-FileHash on the file and compare the result with the one on the release page.

download.why: Foldline is new, and its installer is not code-signed yet, so your browser and Windows have no record of it. The warning means unknown, not dangerous.
safe: Foldline is not a virus and does not bundle other software. It has no account and no ads, and it sends nothing to a Foldline server. The few things it looks up, such as lyrics, weather, a calendar link and the update check, happen only when you use those features, and the Privacy Policy lists each one.
You do not have to take our word for it. The whole app is open source: read the code on GitHub, compare what it does with what we say, or build it yourself.

states.label: States
states.b: pages in one, activities in both
states.p: The notch is open when you point at it and collapsed when you don't. A page fills the open notch. An activity shows in either state.

page.d: One screen of the open notch: media, calendar, timer and more. Switch with the dots in the header, the scroll wheel or the number keys.
page.alt: The media page in the open notch

activity.d: A live signal from your PC or a page, such as a running timer, the battery or a volume change. It shows in the open notch, in the collapsed pill, or only at the moment it happens.

open.d: Small marks sit in the status bar at the top right of the header for as long as something lasts.

collapsed.d: At rest the pill shows the clock, with marks beside it such as the timer ring and the battery ring.

demand.d: Volume, brightness and notifications take over the pill for a moment, then it goes back to rest.

pageDetail.noCollapsed: This page has no activity of its own. It shows only when the notch is open.
pageDetail.noSettings: No settings of its own. Turn the page on and set its place in the Pages section.
pageDetail.exampleNote: An example of what the pill shows.
pageDetail.ctaText: Foldline is free and runs on Windows 10 and 11.
pageDetail.pictureAlt: The {page} page in the open notch

media.lead: The track that is playing, its controls and the synced lyrics, from any player that shows in the Windows media controls.
media.open: Cover art, title and artist, play, pause and skip, and the lyric line that is playing. Lyrics come from LRCLIB.
media.collapsed: A small wave sits in the pill while music plays, so you can see it without opening anything.

shelf.lead: A place to drop files and pick them up later. It holds twelve at most.
shelf.open: Drop a file on the notch to keep it, and drag it out again when you need it.
shelf.collapsed: A short message appears in the pill when something happens on the shelf.

calendar.lead: Your events from an iCal link, by month or by week.
calendar.open: The month or the week, and the events of the day you pick.
calendar.collapsed: A countdown to the next event stays in the pill, so a reminder shows even when the notch is closed.
calendar.settings: The Calendar section sets the view, the iCal address and how often it downloads again.

timer.lead: A focus timer with short and long breaks.
timer.open: Start, pause and reset a round of focus time, then take a short or a long break.
timer.collapsed: A ring in the pill shows the round that is running, and a short message appears when it changes.
timer.settings: The Timer section sets the focus, short break and long break lengths in minutes.

todo.open: Add, tick and remove tasks. Remove one by mistake and you can undo it.

prayer.lead: Prayer times for any city, calculated on your PC.
prayer.open: The prayer times of the day, with the next one marked.
prayer.collapsed: A countdown mark in the pill shows the time to the next prayer, and a message appears when it is time.
prayer.settings: The Shalat section sets the calculation method and the Asr school. The city comes from General.

weather.lead: The next hours or days from MET Norway, for the city you choose.
weather.open: A forecast you can switch between the next hours and the next days.
weather.collapsed: With the rain alert on, a card opens 30 minutes before the next rain, then a countdown mark stays until it starts.
weather.settings: The Weather section holds the rain alert switch. The city comes from General.

stats.lead: CPU, memory, GPUs, network and disks at a glance.
stats.open: Cards for each of them, with charts that update while the page is on screen.
stats.settings: The System stats section picks which disks (up to 3) and which GPUs (up to 2) to show.

clipboard.lead: Your last seven copies, kept in memory only.
clipboard.open: The last seven copies as a list. Nothing is written to disk or sent anywhere, and the history goes when you switch the page off or quit.
clipboard.collapsed: The Copied activity puts a short message in the pill when you copy, with or without this page. It never reads what you copied.

devices.lead: The battery of your Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz receiver devices.
devices.open: Each connected device with its battery level.
devices.collapsed: Two activities work beside this page: a message when a Bluetooth device connects or disconnects, and a red warning when a battery falls to 20 % and 10 %.
